headline: Anthropic staffer claims AI-assisted Riemann proof
pages: Levent Alpoge, a member of Anthropic's technical staff, said Friday that he and the company's Claude AI found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem posed in 1859 about the distribution of prime numbers. He posted a four-page explanation on his website and released the proof as 17 million lines of Lean code, a language that lets computers check mathematical proofs. He said the discovery came late Sunday night, just before Anthropic's stock market debut. Rutgers mathematician Alex Kontorovich said a computer's check is very picky and makes it likely a human reader would also be satisfied, but he still has to do the work of understanding it.

The Clay Mathematics Institute still listed the problem as unsolved hours later. Its president, Martin Bridson, said assessing such a claim takes time. The problem is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems with a $1 million reward. Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment. Source: NPR.
